# Didache Chapter 6 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_006_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 6

**1** See that no one causes you to err from this way of the teaching, since he who does so teaches you apart from God.

**2** For if you are able to bear the whole yoke of the Lord, you will be perfect; but if you are not able, do what you can.

**3** Now concerning food — bear what you are able; but from that which is sacrificed to idols, keep yourself entirely — for it is worship of dead gods.

---

*EMET notes: V.1 — "teaches apart from God" (ἐκτὸς θεοῦ) = outside of/without God. V.2 — "yoke of the Lord" = a Jewish metaphor for Torah observance, here applied to the full ethical teaching of the Didache (chs. 1–5). "Perfect" (τέλειος) — same word as 1:4. The accommodation ("do what you can") is a pastoral concession, likely for Gentile converts. V.3 — "sacrificed to idols" = εἰδωλόθυτος (cf. 1 Cor 8; Rev 2:14, 20). "Worship of dead gods" (λατρεία γάρ ἐστιν θεῶν νεκρῶν) — the idol-food prohibition is grounded in the gods' unreality/death, not merely in social association.*
